bone.purpose: The page ground. Warm off-white, never pure white — white next to ink strobes in sunlight.

paper.purpose: Raised surface on bone: stat cards, secondary buttons, unpaid episode rows.

paper-sunk.purpose: Recessed track: meter and progress rails, skeleton fill, inert discs.

ink.purpose: Settled money and the live viewfinder. Off-black so mint beside it is not punched out.

ink-raised.purpose: One step above ink, for a surface layered inside an ink card.

foreground.purpose: Primary text on bone or paper. 15.25:1 on bone.

muted.purpose: Explanation and secondary copy. 5.98:1 on bone.

subtle.purpose: Footnotes and the .tag caption. 4.89:1 on bone, 4.67:1 on paper.

on-ink.purpose: Primary text inside ink cards and the viewfinder. 17.62:1 on ink.

on-ink-muted.purpose: Secondary text inside ink surfaces and inactive dock tabs. 7.48:1 on ink.

mint.purpose: The task, and money you can act on: what this pays, the withdraw bar, an accepted verdict, the record knob.

mint-ink.purpose: All text on a mint field. 5.96:1 on mint.

lilac.purpose: The model's own reading: task chips, the live prediction thumbnail, the acceptance-rate bar.

lilac-ink.purpose: All text on a lilac field. 5.79:1 on lilac.

butter.purpose: Something needs a hand: insecure connection, in-take coaching, queued uploads, offline.

butter-ink.purpose: All text on a butter field. 5.28:1 on butter.

positive.purpose: Verdict-positive text, drawn from mint so it reads as part of the surface.

caution.purpose: Inline warning text; the same ink as the butter field.

negative.purpose: Used sparingly: the live recording dot, a failed meter segment. Never a panel ground.

figure-hero.purpose: The one number a screen exists to quote: withdrawable balance, an accepted take's payment. One per screen.

figure-lead.purpose: Total earned in the capture header; a screen's secondary quoted amount.

figure-inline.purpose: A figure inside a card: a stat, a per-take amount, the take's remaining seconds.

headline.purpose: The landing page's one sentence. There is no separate display face.

title.purpose: Screen titles, panel headings, the bounty's name.

body.purpose: Explanation, rejection reasons, coaching copy. Capped at max-w-xs / max-w-prose.

label.purpose: The small grey caption naming a figure. Sentence case, never uppercase.

unit.purpose: The small unit sitting on the figure's baseline. Inherits the figure's colour at 72% opacity; floored at 10px.

data.purpose: Geist Mono, scoped to addresses, transaction hashes and sensor measurements only.

shadows.name: lift
shadows.purpose: Default separation of a paper surface from the bone ground, and the viewfinder panel. Panels take shadow, not border.

shadows.name: lift-high
shadows.purpose: Only for something genuinely floating: the record disc straddling the dock, the prediction thumbnail over live video.

lines.name: line
lines.purpose: Hairline divider on bone or paper. Never used to box a card.

motion.name: ease-interactive
motion.purpose: State transitions on .interactive: 200ms for colour/border/shadow, 160ms for transform. Press sinks to scale(0.975).

motion.name: ease-settle
motion.purpose: The one authored moment: a 620ms exponential ease-out arrival.

motion.name: settle
motion.purpose: Panels arrive as a downward cascade from opacity 0 / translateY(14px) / scale(0.985) / blur(6px). Steps settle-1..4 at 40/100/160/220ms. Starts from an already-visible default so a failed animation never costs anyone their balance.

motion.name: shimmer
motion.purpose: Skeletons pulse 0.45 → 0.8 → 0.45 opacity on paper-sunk. Skeletons match the shape of what is loading, never a spinner. Disabled under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.purpose: Every transition, the settle cascade and smooth scrolling live inside this guard. Nothing animates without it.

focus.name: focus-visible
focus.purpose: Keyboard focus. Switches outline-color to #f4f4f1 inside any .on-ink region.

scope.note: The buyer dashboard received a mechanical class sweep onto these tokens (via the --background / --surface / --surface-raised / --accent aliases) so it stays legible on the bone ground. It was not redesigned; its compositions are not evidence of this system.

narrative.overview:
This is a ledger, read outdoors, at arm's length, by somebody who has just taken a phone off their forehead and wants to know what they earned. Everything follows from that scene. The ground is bone — a warm off-white, never pure white, because white next to black strobes in sunlight. The surface is a stack of soft lozenges at a 30px radius, each holding one thing. One figure is quoted at a time, at 600 weight, with a small unit riding its baseline.

It refuses the dark crypto dashboard on purpose: no chart wall, no neon accent, no metric grid, no gradient text. Dark survives in exactly two roles, and in both of them it is a material rather than a theme — the live viewfinder, and the ink cards that hold money that has actually settled. Colour is never decoration here. Three flat pastel fields each own a meaning and are used only where that meaning applies, so a contributor scanning the screen in daylight can tell what a panel is about before reading a word of it.

The world was pinned by a user-supplied reference image (a pastel crypto-wallet UI) rather than chosen by a direction roll, which is why the radii are unusually large and why the palette is a family of flat tints rather than a single accent with neutrals.
keyCharacteristics: Bone ground (#e9e9e6), never pure white, never near-black.
Stacked lozenges: 30px panels, 22px cards, full pills for anything pressable.
Three meaning-bearing fields — mint, lilac, butter — plus ink for settled money.
Figures at 600 weight, tabular, tight tracking, with a small unit on the baseline.
One elevation: a soft offset shadow. Panels take shadow, not border.
One authored motion moment: a four-step downward settle on arrival.

rules.name: The Earned-Colour Rule
rules.body: Nothing is coloured in a field it has not earned. Mint means the task or money you can move; lilac means the model's reading; butter means something needs a hand; ink means money that has settled. A panel that is none of those is paper on bone. Audit test: point at any coloured panel and name which of the four meanings it carries — if you cannot, it should be paper.

rules.name: The Field-Not-Sprinkle Rule
rules.body: A field colours a whole region — a panel, a pill, a card — never a word, an icon, an underline, or a border. There is no accent colour in this system.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor
rules.body: Verified numerically at finish. Body on bone 15.25, muted on bone 5.98, subtle on bone 4.89, subtle on paper 4.67, mint-ink on mint 5.96, lilac-ink on lilac 5.79, butter-ink on butter 5.28, on-ink on ink 17.62, on-ink-muted on ink 7.48. Every pairing clears 4.5:1. Any new pairing must be measured, not assumed.

rules.name: The Quoted Figure Rule
rules.body: A figure is one weight and one size (600, tracking -0.035em, tabular). Its unit is a small rider on the same baseline at 34% of the figure's size, inheriting the figure's colour at 72% opacity — so a unit on mint reads as mint, never as grey punched into it. Never scale the unit by a second type step; never colour it independently.

rules.name: The Cents Knock-Down
rules.body: The cents of a dollar amount drop to 62% opacity, because nobody decides anything on the cents. This is a bone-ground-only device. On the mint fields the same knock-down falls under 3:1 against its own panel, so figures on mint, lilac or butter stay solid.

rules.name: The Tabular Rule
rules.body: Every number in this product is compared against another — frame rates, scores, payments. All of them carry tabular-nums, via .figure, .tabular, or [data-numeric].

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Rule
rules.body: No uppercase labels, no letter-spaced small caps, no kickers or eyebrows. The reference whispers; caps at 11px lose legibility outdoors.

rules.name: The Two-Elevations Rule
rules.body: There are exactly two shadows. If a surface needs to feel deeper, change its tone (bone → paper → ink), do not invent a third shadow.

rules.name: The No-Border Rule
rules.body: Surfaces are separated by tone and shadow. Hairlines exist for dividers and for outlined controls on ink, not for boxing a card.

rules.name: The Pill Rule
rules.body: If it can be pressed, it is a full pill — buttons, chips, tabs, toggles, discs. Rectangles with modest corners are surfaces; pills are controls. The only pressable exception is a whole-surface row, which stays at panel radius because it is a panel.

dos: Do pick a panel's colour from its meaning: mint = the task or money you can move, lilac = the model's reading, butter = needs a hand, ink = settled money. Otherwise paper on bone.
Do quote one figure per screen at 52px, and give it a .tag label above and a .unit rider beside it.
Do use .figure for every amount, score, and count, so columns of numbers do not jitter.
Do put a full pill on anything pressable, and reach for the knob bar when the action is the screen's whole purpose.
Do measure any new colour pairing against the 4.5:1 floor before shipping it; the fields are light and a wrong ink fails immediately.
Do put the primary action in the thumb zone directly above the dock.
Do honour env(safe-area-inset-bottom) on anything fixed to the bottom — this ships as an installed PWA on iOS.
Do wrap every transition and animation in prefers-reduced-motion: no-preference, and start animated elements from a visible default so a failed animation never costs someone their balance.
Do scope Geist Mono to addresses, hashes, and sensor measurements. Everything a person reads is Manrope.
donts: Don't introduce an accent colour, a gradient fill, or a neon. This world refuses the dark crypto dashboard; the four fields are the whole palette.
Don't paint a border on a panel to separate it. Tone and the Lift shadow do that.
Don't invent a third shadow, or stack z-levels. Change the tone instead.
Don't apply .cents on a mint, lilac, or butter ground — the knock-down drops under 3:1 there.
Don't set a label in uppercase or letter-spaced small caps, and don't add a kicker or eyebrow above a heading.
Don't use ink as a background for anything other than settled money, live video, and the dock. It is a material, not a theme.
Don't put a chart wall or a metric grid on a contributor screen. One figure at a time.
Don't shrink the .unit below its 10px floor — a rider on a 17px figure was computing to under 6px before it was floored.
Don't add a second animation. There is one authored moment (.settle), and adding a second one makes the first stop meaning anything.
